gen-silkscreen-gf-fahkwang: Silkscreen spaces its pixel letters so loosely you can nearly feel the gaps. Fahkwang, a plain sans, adds faint pressure shifts in its rounded forms, a gentle, friendly counterweight to all that rigid, constant-width geometry.
gen-silkscreen-gf-figtree: Silkscreen lays its lo-fi, retro letters out like spaghetti, each one holding its own space on the line. Figtree, a plain sans, draws marker-tip shapes with a wide-open e.
gen-silkscreen-gf-finlandica: Retro pixel charm, loud and a little goofy. Finlandica, a sans with open-mouthed e crossbars and an outline you could trace with a fingertip, steadies the whole thing.
gen-silkscreen-gf-fustat: Fustat bends its lines like rope or tubing. Against Silkscreen's spaced-out, lo-fi display letters, that smooth modern flow becomes the pair's strongest quality, with the c left wide open.
gen-silkscreen-gf-gantari: Gantari looks wire-bent from end to end, its wide c apertures giving a friendly, contemporary feel under the headline. Silkscreen's retro display letters sit above it, chunky and spaced out.
gen-silkscreen-gf-gayathri: Round letters whose rims match their stems give Silkscreen its blocky, lo-fi look. Gayathri, a plain sans with open curves and mild letterpress-style thick-thin shifts, softens it, so a larger heading size feels natural.
gen-silkscreen-gf-google-sans: Silkscreen spaces every retro letter so widely you can almost feel the gaps between them. Google Sans, a plain sans with no thick-thin shifts and pulled-back terminals, calms the page and lets the heading stay playful.
gen-silkscreen-gf-google-sans-flex: Google Sans Flex ends every stroke as if cut from one ribbon, each curve closing on a clean, open gap. Reading it feels smooth and modern, a quiet counterpart to Silkscreen's lo-fi heading.
gen-silkscreen-gf-gothic-a1: Gothic A1 reads approachable and businesslike, its c terminal splayed open. Silkscreen does the retro, joint-sharp display work, while the sans-serif body handles the quiet, steady text.
gen-silkscreen-gf-gotu: Clean and modern, Gotu keeps things tidy. Beneath it all, Silkscreen's monoline retro letters add a lo-fi spark, while Gotu's sturdy hairlines and open-mouthed e crossbars carry the text.
